newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU seen importing more vegetable oils in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: EU seen importing more vegetable oils in 1996/97.

text.p: European Union imports of vegetable oils from third countries will rise in 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) as a result of lower domestic seed crops, the independent newsletter Oil World said in its latest report, issued earlier this week.
Oil World pegged 1996/97 imports of 17 oils and fats by the EU-15 at 4.53 million tonnes, compared with 4.28 million in 1995/96.
Crushings of domestic and imported seed were also seen rising.
Domestic EU supplies from 1996/97 crops and stocks would be down by three percent from 1995/96 at 15.1 million tonnes, mostly due to rapeseed crop losses in Germany and Scandinavia, the report said.
But EU seed crushings were forecast 300,000 tonnes above the 1995/96 figure at 28.5 million tonnes in 1996/97.
Soybean imports from third countries for crushing in the EU were forecast to rise to 15.4 million tonnes in 1996/97, up 1.2 million from the previous season.
